newsitem.title: GHANA: COCOA -- Little policy shift seen at new Ghana board.
newsitem.headline: COCOA -- Little policy shift seen at new Ghana board.

text.p: Senior officials at the Ghana Cocoa Marketing Board (COCOBOD) expect no major policy shifts following a change of leadership at the agency.
President Jerry Rawlings last week named John Henry Newman, an executive from the buying subsidiary of Cocobod, as the group's new chief executive.

Rawlings named traditional chief Jacob Somiah Odeneho Ababio II as chairman of the COCOBOD's newly reconstituted Board of Directors. He also transferred supervision of cocoa affairs from his office to the Ministry of Finance.
The shuffle followed a probe into the affairs of senior COCOBOD officials and staff from the president's office after allegations by private newspapers of corruption in the industry.
"We are not expecting great changes in the policy of Cocobod as he (Newman) is a man of the house," said a senior Cocobod official who asked not to be named.
Newman had held his previous post since 1988 after joining the board in 1979.
World Bank expert Richard Epworth said the Bank would like to see significant liberalisation of commodity marketing.

"Our position is that we would like the marketing of products like coffee and cocoa liberalized to the maximum extent possible," he told Reuters, adding that he did not see the reshuffle as aimed at such change.
He said he expected policy direction to come from a UK consultant's report on reorganisation and liberalisation of cocoa exports.
"The situation at the moment is that the Ministry of Finance commissioned a report to LMC in the UK which we financed, and that final report has only just come out," he said.
LMC is part of UK consulting firm Landell Mills.
"We haven't discussed it yet with the government. The government has set up a task-force to review the outcome of the report," Epworth said

He added - "It is simply looking at the circumstances of the cocoa industry in Ghana and also looking at the possibilities of liberalising the export of cocoa crop and drawing upon examples of neighbouring countries and other countries in the world which have done a similar sort of thing and coming up with number of options that might suit Ghana."
"I think it will also become a topic of public discussion. It's such a major factor in the Ghanaian economy, I wouldn't expect any action to be taken without a public discussion," Epworth said.

He confirmed that a department of Cocobod, Cocoa Services Division which deals with field services, would be transferred soon to the Ministry of Agriculture, to be merged with the ministry's non-cocoa agriculture extension services.
The announcement of this merger was made in February by Finance Minister Kwame Peprah in his budget statement.
